PullRequest.Title: ci: shard Electron smoke tests across two jobs per platform
PullRequest.Body:

Refs #341382

The Electron smoke tests are the slowest PR job on all three platforms. On the slower Linux runners they take about 20 minutes and keep hitting the smoke step's 20 minute timeout. This PR splits them into two shards per platform. The required checks keep their names, so branch protection doesn't change.

## Changes

- **New `--shard <index>/<total>` runner option**, in `test/smoke/src/shard.ts`.
  - Each top-level suite runs in exactly one shard. Suites are assigned longest first, using a small table of estimated CI durations.
  - Suites whose tests are all skipped on the current platform count as zero (for example, Terminal on Linux).
  - An out-of-date estimate only makes the shards uneven; it never skips a suite.
- **Matrix shards:** `pr.yml` runs the Electron smoke tests as a two-shard matrix per platform. The shards report as `<OS> (shard 1/2) / Electron-Smoke` and `<OS> (shard 2/2) / Electron-Smoke`.
- **Gate job:** a matrix gate job, `electron-smoke-checks`, reports the existing required `<OS> / Electron-Smoke` checks. A platform's check fails if any of its shards did not succeed.
- **Placement tied to the workflows:**
  - On Windows, WSL is set up only in shard 1, and the WSL Dev Container suite is pinned there. `VSCODE_SMOKE_TEST_WSL_REQUIRED` stays set in every shard so all shards register the same suites and compute the same split.
  - On macOS, the PAC proxy Agents Window runs happen only in the last shard, and the balancer reserves about 270s for them there.
- **Duration summary:** the runner prints each top-level suite's duration at the end of a run, so the estimate table is easy to update.
- **Docs:** updated the smoke-tests skill and the smoke README.

## Expected impact

These estimates use the per-suite timings from run [38443277116](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38443277116):

| Platform | Smoke step today | Slower shard (estimated) |
|---|---|---|
| Linux | 1179s | ~591s |
| macOS (incl. proxy runs) | ~1027s | ~551s |
| Windows (incl. WSL setup) | ~1024s | ~546s |

## Notes for reviewers

- Every shard must register the same list of suites; otherwise suites can be skipped or run twice. Don't make suite registration depend on anything that differs between shards.
- Artifact names and the Windows `JobId` runner label get a `-shard<N>` suffix.
- Each extra shard repeats about 1.5–3.5 minutes of job setup. That includes one more macOS xlarge runner per run.
- This doesn't address the roughly 6 seconds each app launch got slower around Sep 16, which the issue also describes.

## How to test

Run one shard locally with `npm run smoketest -- --shard 1/2`. This PR's CI exercises the sharded jobs end to end.

Validation done:

- `node ../../node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc6` (in `test/smoke`): passed.
- Throwaway mocha dry-run harness over the compiled runner, with `VSCODE_QUALITY=oss VSCODE_SMOKE_TEST_POLICY=1` and `--shard` values `1/2`, `2/2`, `1/3`, `2/3`, `3/3` and `1/1`. Run both with and without `VSCODE_SMOKE_TEST_WSL_REQUIRED=1`. **Passed:** shards never overlap and together match the unsharded list of 132 tests, `1/1` matches the unsharded run, and the WSL suite always lands in shard 1.
- `--shard` values `0/2`, `3/2`, `1/0`, `abc` and `2` each exit with code 1 and a clear message: passed.
- The end-of-run duration summary, checked against fake suites including a failing run: passed. The exit codes are unchanged.
- `npm run eslint -- test/smoke/src/shard.ts test/smoke/src/main.ts test/smoke/test/index.js`: passed.
- `node build/hygiene.ts` on the changed files: passed.
- `actionlint -shellcheck= .github/workflows/pr.yml .github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml .github/workflows/pr-darwin-test.yml .github/workflows/pr-win32-test.yml`: no new findings. The only findings are 6 existing warnings about unknown self-hosted runner labels.
- Not run locally: the smoke tests themselves, because they launch VS Code windows.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pull-request Electron smoke tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each platform, both shard jobs must provision a runner, check out the repository, restore/install dependencies, transpile and compile test assets, set up Electron, compile smoke tests, run their assigned top-level suites, and upload results. The new required-check gates start only after all Linux, macOS, and Windows shard groups finish, so merge readiness remains gated by the slowest platform plus a small gate-job startup. The duplicated setup is on each shard's critical path; the two shards execute in parallel.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provision two fresh workspaces per platform and perform LFS repository checkout in each shard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two checkouts per platform, six total for the Electron smoke scenario; previously one per platform, three total.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One Electron smoke job and one checkout ran per platform.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each shard cannot begin setup until its checkout completes; shard checkouts can run concurrently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run apt update/install and start Linux display services in every Linux shard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two apt setup sequences for the two Linux shards; previously one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The single Linux smoke job performed this system setup once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is repeated on both Linux shard critical paths, but the paths run concurrently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore and extract the node_modules cache and restore the built-in extensions cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Each of the six shard jobs performs one restore for each cache. Warm runs download/extract the same platform cache twice; cold misses cause each shard to run its platform dependency installation independently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each platform's single smoke job restored or installed each cache once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cache restore or cold installation blocks each shard's compilation. Parallel jobs avoid serial fan-out, though they increase aggregate network and filesystem traffic.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transpile the client/extensions, set up Electron, compile extension fixtures, compile the smoke runner, and compile the Copilot extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The full setup sequence now runs twice per platform, once per shard; previously once per platform.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The single platform job compiled these assets once before running all suites.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: CPU and filesystem work blocks each shard before test execution, but both shard sequences run concurrently. This is the explicit fixed setup cost exchanged for shorter suite execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: test/smoke/src/main.ts:281-301 and root before hook at 402-425
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clone or refresh the vscode-smoketest-express test repository in each smoke process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One clone per shard process, two per platform and six total in PR CI; previously one per platform and three total. Each fresh job starts with a new temporary test directory, so there is no cross-job warm repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The one smoke process per platform cloned the test repository once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The root setup hook blocks all assigned suites in each shard; clones occur concurrently across jobs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch VS Code and execute only the top-level suites selected for the shard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Each registered top-level suite is assigned to exactly one of two shards. Effective suite/test cardinality across both shards remains the unsharded set; root setup occurs once in each process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All top-level suites ran serially in one process per platform.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Suite execution is the dominant work this change parallelizes, reducing the slower shard toward half of the previous serial suite duration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install Squid if needed and run the two PAC proxy Agents Window invocations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Still one Squid setup and two proxy invocations total, now confined to the last macOS shard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same setup and two invocations followed the single macOS smoke run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These remain on the macOS critical path, and the balancer reserves their estimated duration in the last shard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore/install WSL support and provision the WSL Dev Container fixture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Still one WSL setup total because only shard 1 executes it; the WSL suite is pinned to shard 1.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The single Windows smoke job provisioned WSL once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks Windows shard 1 only and therefore can determine the slower Windows shard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provision three Ubuntu gate jobs that translate shard group results to the existing required-check names.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three small gate jobs per PR, one per required OS check; previously the platform jobs themselves supplied those checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No separate gate runners were needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All three wait for every platform shard group and add runner queue/startup plus one shell command after the slowest group.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The matrix fixes effective concurrency at two shards per platform. Test execution scales with the number and measured duration of top-level suites, each assigned once. Repeated setup, cache, checkout, and root-hook work scales linearly with shard count, currently doubling from one to two.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Two shard jobs run independently per platform, for up to six Electron smoke jobs across the workflow. GitHub Actions runner availability supplies backpressure; there is no in-workflow shared limiter. Suites are serial within each Mocha process. The three gate matrix jobs start after all shard groups complete.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm runs restore the same platform node_modules and built-in-extension caches independently in both shards; cold misses make both shards install dependencies/download extensions concurrently. Suite balancing uses a small in-memory static duration map and no persisted runtime cache. WSL setup remains single-shard, and macOS proxy work remains single-shard.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the duplicated boundaries and two-way concurrency because the matrix and reusable workflow steps are explicit. High confidence that actual top-level test suites are partitioned exactly once by the assignment/filter logic.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Aggregate runner minutes, network bytes, and setup CPU increase materially, but repository evidence does not establish runner-pool saturation or a user-visible throughput/queue regression. The critical-path suite duration is intentionally reduced, and the shard count is bounded at two.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff intentionally trades bounded duplicate setup and additional runner capacity for a substantially shorter smoke-test critical path. Without evidence that the extra six-way capacity causes queueing or lowers PR throughput, the aggregate-cost increase alone does not meet the performance finding standard.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local smoke-test execution with and without --shard
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The process parses the shard, registers all Mocha suites, computes one assignment over the suite tree, creates temporary test data, runs the root setup hook including the test-repository clone, then executes only selected suites. Without --shard or with 1/1, no suite filtering occurs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove/create a temporary smoke-test directory and extension directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per runner process, unchanged for an unsharded invocation; one per explicitly launched shard process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every smoke runner process already recreated its temporary directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous setup occurs before suite execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clone or fetch/reset the smoke-test repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per process. A user launching two shards creates two processes and therefore two clones; a normal unsharded run remains one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An unsharded local invocation cloned once; there was no supported multi-process shard workflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The root hook blocks all selected suites.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Assignment work traverses the registered suite/test tree once and then selects among the requested shard count. For the documented realistic input of two shards and the repository's bounded smoke suite list, CPU and allocation are negligible relative to app launches.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One Mocha process executes suites serially. Running multiple local shard commands concurrently is user-managed; the code adds no internal worker pool or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each process recreates its temporary directory, so the test repository is cold per process. The static duration estimate map is initialized once per process. There is no cross-process coalescing or cache introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from parseShard/selectShardSuites and the root setup hook call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users could request unusually large shard totals, but the supported/documented path uses small totals and no realistic performance trigger was found for the assignment algorithm.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Existing unsharded behavior is preserved, and realistic sharded use adds bounded linear assignment work while intentionally distributing expensive suites.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Runner listeners record a timestamp at each runnable top-level suite start and append one duration at suite end. After Mocha completes, the bounded duration array is sorted and printed before process exit; formatting is off the test-execution critical path except for the final completion callback.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: State and final sort scale with the number of executed top-level suites in one shard, not tests, frames, or process lifetime. The process exits immediately after reporting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mocha emits events synchronously in one process; no added parallel work or queue exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache. The map and array live only for one smoke runner process and are reclaimed at exit.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the two runner event handlers and completion callback.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact suite count can evolve, but it is a small, repository-defined collection and each suite contributes one map entry and one result object.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Retention and sorting are bounded by top-level suites and cannot accumulate across runs.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and relevant workflow/runner call paths. The change partitions smoke suites while duplicating bounded per-job setup across two concurrent shards; this is an explicit latency/capacity tradeoff, not a demonstrated performance regression. Cache, subprocess, network, filesystem, concurrency, and lifecycle behavior were checked, and no high-confidence actionable performance issue was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
